item.title: Mickelson Pumpkin Patch in Petaluma — Fri Oct 16, 9:00 AM — Mickelson Pumpkin Patch 5495 Redwood Highway
item.description:
Celebrate fall at Mickelson Pumpkin Patch in Petaluma, just north of the Marin-Sonoma county line! This family-friendly pumpkin patch offers plenty of fall fun, including pumpkin picking, a hay maze and pyramid, tractor rides, a paintball gallery, and more. Shop for pumpkins, squash, and gourds, and enjoy food vendors and craft beer for the grown-ups. Admission: Monday-Friday: FREE Saturday-Sunday: $5 per person Additional fees apply for select activities. Please note: No outside food or dogs allowed. Directions: To get there, take Highway 101 north to the Petaluma Boulevard South/Kastania Road exit \(Exit 472A\). Turn right at the stoplight then turn right onto Petaluma Boulevard South. Follow the road south until you get to the pumpkin patch, which will be on your left.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Nicasio Valley Pumpkin Patch — Fri Oct 16, 10:00 AM — Nicasio Valley Pumpkin Patch 5300 Nicasio Valley Road
item.description:
Located in the small west Marin village of Nicasio, the farm is just west of the Nicasio Village Square right on Nicasio Valley Road. Nicasio Valley Pumpkin Patch is open seven days a week through Halloween from 10 am to 6 pm weekends and 10 am to 4 pm during the week, and it's always worth a visit. It's been a Marin County tradition for over 20 years! Nicasio Valley Pumpkin Patch offers a wide variety of pumpkins spread out in an expansive meadow on the farm. Pumpkin varieties ranged from your standard Halloween jack-o-lantern types to white ones, green Italian and Australian varieties, and flat European "Cinderella" style squash. The farmstand also offers of gourds, squash, and decorative cornstalks, apples, as well as drinks and snacks. Pumpkins range in price from $8 to $44. Admission is Free, Pumpkins are Priced Individually
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market — Sat Oct 17, 12:00 AM — Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
item.description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. item.title: Harvest Table at Somerston Estate — Sat Oct 17, 12:00 PM — Somerston Estate
item.description:
Harvest is drawing to a close, and there’s no better time to experience the culmination of the season at Somerston Estate. Join us for an unforgettable afternoon featuring a seasonal lunch expertly paired with estate wines, all set against the stunning backdrop of our vineyards as another remarkable vintage nears completion.
Executive Winemaker Cody Hurd will join us to reflect on the season’s triumphs and challenges, sharing insights from the harvest along with a special harvest-inspired experience exclusive to the day. From the final fruit coming in to stories from the cellar, this is a rare opportunity to connect with the people and passion behind every bottle.
Raise a glass to another extraordinary harvest while enjoying exceptional food, world-class wines, and the unparalleled beauty of Somerston Estate.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Reuse in Art, Reuse in Life: A Conversation Between Ali Gass and Phoebe Schenker — Sun Oct 18, 3:30 PM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join Alison Gass, Founding Executive Director of the ICA San Francisco, and Phoebe Schenker, Executive Director of Reuse Alliance, for a wide-ranging conversation about reuse in contemporary and historical art and why it is more relevant than ever.
The discussion will explore the many ways artists have engaged with reuse, from incorporating found and reclaimed materials to making reuse itself a central subject of their work. Together, Gass and Schenker will consider how reuse connects to broader cultural conversations about creativity, sustainability, consumption, and value, while also exploring how reuse can become a creative practice in our own everyday lives.

item.title: Hosting 101 at Great Company — Thu Oct 22, 6:00 PM — Great Company
item.description:
You’ve said “we should get together” a hundred times. This is the class where you actually do it.
Hosting isn’t about a perfect house, matching napkins, or a fancy menu. It’s about opening the door and making people feel glad they came. Over one relaxed evening around our table, we’ll walk through the whole arc of having people over: who to invite and how to ask, how to set up so you’re not stuck in the kitchen, and what to do in those first awkward ten minutes when everyone arrives.
Then we’ll make dinner without turning on a stove. In small groups, you’ll build a generous spread. Think bread, cheese, tinned fish, pickles, something sweet. You’ll learn how much to buy, how to make a board look abundant, and how to make an evening come together with ease. Then we’ll all sit down and eat what we made.
Before you leave, you’ll pick a date and send a real invitation. Yes, really. We’ll help you write it.
